context: Either make the finding_links -> items edge ON DELETE SET NULL / CASCADE, or include finding-link cleanup in the replace path. Whichever is chosen, rehearse on a restored local snapshot first (todo_db_shadow.py + restore-legacy), then apply with an audit verify.
description:
chatgpt-codex-connector review finding on merged PR #1273 (P2, _project/scripts/todo_findings.py:87). Deferred from the PR-review sweep in PR #1292 because the fix implies a hosted-database migration, which is out of scope for a code-fix sweep; tracked in GitHub issue #1293.

When a finding is linked/promoted to an item, the FK is stored in finding_links. Hosted bulk_transfer(..., replace=True) deletes only TRANSFER_TABLES in _project/scripts/todo_db.py, and that list intentionally EXCLUDES all findings tables. In a tracker that has any promoted/linked finding, a hosted YAML --replace reload will therefore either fail when DELETE FROM items hits the retained FK, or leave a stale link to an item that was replaced if the pipeline connection is not enforcing FKs.
Thread: https://github.com/joeharris76/BenchBox/pull/1273#discussion_r3640659592

MIGRATION RISK: this touches the shared hosted (Turso) tracker. Rehearse against a restored snapshot before touching production, and confirm the restore drill in docs/operations/todo-db-benchbox-extraction.md still passes afterwards.

anti_patterns.dont: apply the migration directly against the production hosted tracker before rehearsing
anti_patterns.instead: rehearse on a restored snapshot, then apply with audit verify
anti_patterns.why: a bad FK migration on the shared tracker is hard to reverse

anti_patterns.dont: issue raw DELETE statements against the hosted DB
anti_patterns.why: the tracker classifier blocks raw DELETEs and row-by-row bulk writes

preserves.behavior: Existing promoted/linked findings survive the migration with their links intact
The documented restore + audit verify drill still passes after the change

work_units.evidence: Reproduced on a seeded local v3 DB: with foreign_keys ON the --replace DELETE loop over reversed(TRANSFER_TABLES) aborts with 'FOREIGN KEY constraint failed'; with FK OFF (the SQLite/libSQL server default) it succeeds leaving 1 stale link and a finding still claiming disposition='promoted' against an unresolvable target.
work_units.summary: Reproduce on a restored local snapshot: promote a finding, then run a --replace reload and capture the failure/stale-link behaviour

work_units.evidence: Implemented in the composed SCHEMA_VERSION 3->4 migration (PR #1347) as DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED on finding_links.target_item, NOT the ON DELETE SET NULL this item's approach suggested: prototyping showed SET NULL nulls target_item even when the reload REINSERTS the item, destroying promote provenance on every reload. Deferring the check to COMMIT lets the legitimate delete-then-reinsert commit with the link intact while a genuine dangler is still refused.
work_units.summary: Implement delete-safety (FK ON DELETE change or replace-path link cleanup) with a schema migration

work_units.evidence: Regression tests pin both directions (reload keeps the link; genuine dangler refused at COMMIT). Rehearsed on a scratch Turso DB: migration preserved all rows and the promote link, and the DEFERRABLE clause is present on the real primary. Production migrated and verified: finding_links carries 'target_item TEXT REFERENCES items(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED', 0 links and all other counts unchanged. 9 restore/transfer tests pass.
work_units.summary: Re-run the restore + audit verify drill on the snapshot and confirm no stale links remain
